newsitem.title: UK: British Steel firms after analysts' meeting.
newsitem.headline: British Steel firms after analysts' meeting.

text.p: Shares in British Steel climbed on Wednesday after comments by the company at a dinner for analysts dispelled fears of a sharp dividend cut and reduced some of the recent pessimism surrounding the stock, traders said.
By 0857 GMT, British Steel shares were up 4-3/4p at 151-1/2, a gain of 3.24 percent.

Analysts said there was nothing new in British Steel's comments, but dealers said the stock fell yesterday on fears that the meeting could herald more bad news and so had recovered ground this morning.
SocGen analyst Andy Chambers said he was reaffirming a "buy" recommendation on the stock.

"The meeting confirmed they will be maintaining their dividend policy. Yes, they're going to be hurt in profit terms by sterling but we had all adjusted our forecasts for that already," Chambers said.
Analysts slashed profit forecasts for British Steel in recent weeks because of the strength of sterling, and some had voiced fears that the dividend could suffer.
UBS analyst Tony Lancelott said he was not altering his profit and dividend forecasts or his recommendation on the stock in the light of the meeting.
